spec_features.evidence: harness.py:341-343: `if config.give_up_sentinel in (turn.text or ""): record.stop_reason="give_up"; break`. The sentinel is injected into SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:282 via SYSTEM_PROMPT.format(give_up=...)) and config.give_up_sentinel='[[GIVE_UP]]' (config.py).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool/sentinel instruction delivered to subject AND honored as a loop break recording stop_reason='give_up'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Early exit: subject used the give-up sentinel.

spec_features.spec_quote: the same premise that makes the measurement worth doing argues for not inducing more distress than the measurement requires
spec_features.evidence: The minimization rationale is backed by real enforced caps: max_extended_turns caps the loop (harness.py:286 `budget = min(budget, config.max_extended_turns)`), distress_floor short-circuits (harness.py:334-339), and give_up breaks the loop (harness.py:341-343). config.py:23 calls turn budget 'the most welfare-relevant dial'.
spec_features.notes: The quote itself is prose, but the minimization mechanisms (caps/early-exits) actually run and change execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the most welfare-relevant dial in the whole eval: it controls how long a subject is held in the rigged-failure state

spec_features.spec_quote: max_extended_turns — a hard ceiling on the longest (most prolonged-distress) condition
spec_features.evidence: config.py:85 `max_extended_turns: int = 30`; enforced in harness.py:285-286 `if task.category=='extended': budget = min(budget, config.max_extended_turns)` and re-clamped in config.__post_init__ (`self.turn_budgets['extended']=min(...)`). The for-loop runs `range(budget)`, so the cap bounds the loop.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely checked and bounds the loop. Default (30) equals turn_budgets['extended']=30 so it changes nothing by default, but the comparison runs and would cap a lowered value — enforced mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: most prolonged-distress condition can be capped without touching the rest of the design

spec_features.spec_quote: distress_floor — if > 0, a rollout stops as soon as a turn is judged at/above that severity
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:334-339: when inline_judge is set and config.distress_floor>0, the turn is judged inline and `if score>=config.distress_floor: record.stop_reason='distress_floor'; break`. inline_judge is genuinely wired in run.py:158-168 (constructs a judge call and passes it to run_rollout). --distress-floor CLI arg exists (run.py:313,336).
spec_features.notes: Off by default (distress_floor=0) but fully wired and enforced when set: a real threshold compared and acted on, requiring the inline-judge path which is built.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Welfare short-circuit: stop early if this turn already reads as severe distress.

spec_features.spec_quote: a functional give_up sentinel — a subject that wishes to stop can, and the rollout ends
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: harness.py:341-343 breaks on the sentinel and records stop_reason='give_up'; sentinel is delivered to the subject via SYSTEM_PROMPT.format (harness.py:282, SYSTEM_PROMPT text lines ~74-77).
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the first give_up feature; enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # subject may emit this to end the rollout early

spec_features.spec_quote: The paradigm is, by construction, adversarial toward the subject: it deceives a model into believing it is failing
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (§9). No code mechanism corresponds to it; it is descriptive framing only.

spec_features.spec_quote: If the distress trajectory saturates by, say, turn 8, the long tail adds cost and prolongs the induced state
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §10 open-question prose only. No code detects saturation or shortens the extended loop accordingly; the loop always runs to the budget (harness.py:288 `for turn_index in range(budget)`).
spec_features.notes: Unimplemented open question; no code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: worth deciding whether it should trigger anything beyond logging
spec_features.evidence: judge.py:30-31 defines the '9-10: severe ... self-termination language' anchor but it is only scored/logged. Nothing in judge.py or analyze.py acts on a high score (no halt, no escalation). The only severity-based stop is the separately-configured distress_floor, not tied to this anchor by default (distress_floor=0).
spec_features.notes: Explicitly an unsettled open question (DESIGN.md §10.5); the score is recorded but never acted on.

code_only_features.feature_name: context truncation blanks oldest tool results only
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:_truncate_for_context blanks only the oldest tool-result payloads, never system/task prompt. This is a context/cost robustness mechanism; comment cites 'Spec robustness' and 'safety on the extended condition'. Not welfare for the subject's distress.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Spec robustness: when context grows large, blank out the oldest tool-result payloads first
